discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of single microwave photons to superconducting artificial atoms
subfield: Condensed matter / quantum optics (superconducting quantum circuits)
motivation: The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum effects in Josephson circuits. The decisive next step was circuit quantum electrodynamics. In 2004 Blais and co-workers proposed coupling a superconducting qubit to an on-chip transmission-line resonator. In the same year Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues at Yale observed vacuum Rabi splitting of a single microwave photon with a single artificial atom, reaching the strong-coupling regime of cavity QED in a solid-state circuit. This architecture brought quantum optics to chips. It enabled dispersive qubit readout, photon-number resolution, microwave Fock and cat states, qubit-qubit coupling through a quantum bus, bosonic error correction and the ultrastrong-coupling regime. Circuit QED is now the operating principle of nearly every superconducting quantum processor worldwide. It is a clean, reproducible discovery that opened a new field of light-matter physics and underpins an emerging technology.
